In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the contraindications for MPH medication are relevant in clinical practice and whether the contraindicated conditions are over-represented in MPH users.
the safety and effectiveness of ADHD medications in children and adolescents.
the identification of subgroups of children with ADHD that may be at higher risk of adverse drug reactions to MPH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MPH treatment in children is associated with a high risk of comorbidities.

in a substantial proportion of children who are started on methylphenidate there is a pre-existing record of a psychiatric disorder and that in this subgroup of patients the presence of cerebro- and/or cardiovascular comorbidity has to be carefully evaluated.
the risks of MPH medication should be weighed carefully against the risks of an untreated ADHD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of ADHD in Germany is about 3.2%, and about 1.5 % of all children and teenagers are treated with MPH.

the risk of cardiovascular events with MPH treatment is small in general and that the presence of a cardiovascular comorbidity does not necessarily exclude MPH treatment in the absence of a history of cardiovascular events.
the use of MPH is a common treatment in Germany and is often used in children who have a comorbidity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MPH is a very effective medication for children with ADHD and that its benefits outweigh its risks.

the prevalence and incidence of MPH treatment is high in children and that a substantial proportion of MPH users have psychiatric comorbidities, but only a minority have a record of a cardiovascular comorbidity.
the use of a database with a broad range of information is a powerful tool in assessing comorbidities in a large number of patients.
